LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is being parsed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, which only executes code in the global/top-level scope. The top level of this file contains only standard variable assignments (pkgname, pkgdesc, pkgver, url, license, arch, depends, options), the source_url definitions using string interpolation from the declared GitHub author/repository, and a sha256sums entry for x86_64. There is no command substitution ($()), backtick execution, pipe-to-shell pattern (curl|bash), eval/base64 obfuscation, or network fetch executed at top level. All of these variables are simple assignments that just set string values, and the source URLs resolve to the project's own GitHub releases (https://github.com/iorinu/termrain/releases/), which is consistent with standard AUR packaging practice for a -bin package.

The package() function and its install commands run during build/package phases, not during sourcing for --printsrcinfo, so they are out of scope for this specific gate. No top-level code exfiltrates data, executes downloaded content, or performs unexpected file modifications.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>
Top-level code only standard variable assignments and source URL definitions.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
